To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the win-back strategy has different effects on consumers' reinitiating brand–consumer relationship intention (CIRR) and that the effects depend on the type of win-back strategy and brand relationship quality.
win-back strategies have a positive impact on reinitiating BCR and that the effect is moderated by brand-relationship quality.
the three commonly adopted strategies of apology, privilege, and tangible reward have differential effects on consumers’ CIRR, and that brand-relationship quality moderates this relationship.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to effectively reinitiate BCR and the conditions that affect the effectiveness of win-back strategies.
a neglected topic, namely how to re-establish a BCR with consumers who have been lost.
the effects of win-back strategies and the moderating role played by brand relationship quality on consumers’ intention to reinitiate a relationship with a transgressing brand.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

win-back investment is a useful strategy to reinitiate brand-consumer relationship, and the effect of this investment depends on the type of win-back strategy adopted, as well as the quality of brand relationship prior to brand transgressions.
the effects of win-back strategies on CIRR are moderated by consumers’ brand-relationship quality, which in turn is moderated by the severity of the transgression.

win-back strategy has a positive effect on consumers’ intention to reinitiate relationship with transgression brands; and the positive effect will be more prominent if the relationship quality prior to brand’s transgression is high.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of win back strategies on reinitiating BCR is contingent on brand relationship quality.
the win-back strategies of apology, privilege and tangible rewards have different effects on CIRR and the effect of win back strategies is moderated by brand relationship quality.

the effect of win back strategies on reinitiating relationship is not a one-way process, it depends on consumers’ prior perception of the relationship with the brand and the type of win-back strategy that the transgression brand employs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
win-back strategies are not equally effective for different consumers, and the effect is contingent on brand relationship quality.
brand managers should not treat all consumers equally in their win-back strategy.
brand managers should consider the level of relationship quality when designing win-back strategies.
